tag.title: How nom::bytes::complete::tag works
tag.description: Matches an exact piece of text at the start of the input.

slides.caption: Every nom parser takes the input and returns Ok((what is left, what it parsed)) or an error.
"GET" is at the start: it is consumed.
The rest of the input comes back first.
If the text does not start with "GET", the result is Err(Error(.., Tag)).

take-while1.title: How nom::bytes::complete::take_while1 works
take-while1.description: Takes the longest prefix whose characters pass a test (at least one).

slides.caption: An empty run is an error here.
Fails if the input is shorter.

take-until.title: How nom::bytes::complete::take_until works
take-until.description: Takes everything up to (not including) a pattern.

slides.caption: Fails if the pattern never appears.
The delimiter stays in the input.
Returns the text as written in the input.
Useful for SQL or HTTP headers.
Combine with map_res to get a number.
An empty match is an error.

multispace0.title: How nom::character::complete::multispace0 works
multispace0.description: Zero or more spaces, tabs and line breaks.

slides.caption: Never fails: zero whitespace is fine.
space0 skips only spaces and tabs.

one-of.title: How nom::character::complete::one_of works
one-of.description: Matches one character from a set.

alphanumeric1.title: How nom::character::complete::alphanumeric1 works
alphanumeric1.description: One or more ASCII letters or digits.

slides.caption: Stops at the first other character.

map-res.title: How nom::combinator::map_res works
map-res.description: Applies a function that may fail to a parser's output.

slides.caption: digit1 gives the digits as text; map_res turns them into a u32, and a failed conversion becomes a parse error.
map() is the version for functions that cannot fail.
The function cannot fail; use map_res if it can.

opt.title: How nom::combinator::opt works
opt.description: Makes a parser optional: Some(output) or None, never an error.

slides.caption: Common for signs and optional fields.

value.title: How nom::combinator::value works
value.description: Returns a fixed value when the parser succeeds.

slides.caption: The matched text is thrown away.

recognize.title: How nom::combinator::recognize works
recognize.description: Returns the input text a parser consumed, instead of its output.

slides.caption: Handy to grab a whole token made of several parts.
consumed() returns both text and output.

all-consuming.title: How nom::combinator::all_consuming works
all-consuming.description: Fails unless the parser uses up the whole input.

slides.caption: Use it at the top level of a parser.
Without it trailing junk is silently ignored.

verify.title: How nom::combinator::verify works
verify.description: Runs a parser, then checks its output with a condition.

slides.caption: The input is not consumed when the check fails.

delimited.title: How nom::sequence::delimited works
delimited.description: Parses open, content and close, keeping only the content.

slides.caption: Three parsers run in order; the first and last results are thrown away.
"42" is kept, ")" is matched and dropped.
preceded and terminated drop only one side.

preceded.title: How nom::sequence::preceded works
preceded.description: Parses a prefix, then keeps only what follows.

slides.caption: terminated keeps the first part instead.

terminated.title: How nom::sequence::terminated works
terminated.description: Parses something followed by a terminator, keeping the first part.

slides.caption: Common for line or statement endings.

separated-pair.title: How nom::sequence::separated_pair works
separated-pair.description: Parses two values with a separator between them.

slides.caption: A tuple (a, b, c) of parsers runs them all in order.

pair.title: How nom::sequence::pair works
pair.description: Runs two parsers in order and returns both outputs.

slides.caption: In nom 8 a tuple (p1, p2) works the same.

alt.title: How nom::branch::alt works
alt.description: Tries parsers in order and returns the first that succeeds.

slides.caption: If a branch fails, the next one is tried on the same input. If none work, alt fails.
Order matters: put longer or more specific branches first.

separated-list1.title: How nom::multi::separated_list1 works
separated-list1.description: One or more items with a separator between them.

slides.caption: Parses an item, then repeatedly a separator and another item, until that fails.
The items are collected in a Vec.
separated_list0 also accepts an empty list.

many0.title: How nom::multi::many0 works
many0.description: Repeats a parser zero or more times, collecting the results.

slides.caption: Stops at the first failure; zero matches is fine.

many1.title: How nom::multi::many1 works
many1.description: Repeats a parser one or more times.

slides.caption: Fails if the first attempt fails.

fold-many0.title: How nom::multi::fold_many0 works
fold-many0.description: Repeats a parser and folds the results, without building a Vec.

slides.caption: The initial value is created by a closure.

count.title: How nom::multi::count works
count.description: Runs a parser exactly n times.

slides.caption: Fails if fewer than n succeed.

parser-parse.title: How nom::Parser::parse works
parser-parse.description: Runs any parser (function or combinator) on an input.

slides.caption: In nom 8 combinators return a Parser; call .parse(input) on them.
parse_complete treats the input as final.
